date_note: Mirage News's page is dated 24 November and says the Federal Court ordered the penalty; it gives no earlier day for the order.
exec: Australia's prudential regulator has won an $8 million penalty against Bendigo Bank over a 2023 cyber incident; APRA says it expects its regulated entities to have robust cyber protection systems.
geo_basis: bank and regulator are Australian; pin set to Bendigo, Victoria, the bank's home city (not stated on the pages)
plain: A court ordered Bendigo Bank to pay $8 million after APRA brought a case over a 2023 cyber incident at its Alliance Bank business. APRA says it expects regulated entities to have robust cyber protection systems.
summary: Mirage News reports that the Federal Court ordered Bendigo and Adelaide Bank to pay $8 million for breaching the Banking Executive Accountability Regime after a 2023 cyber incident. APRA's August release says an attacker gained access to approximately 257 customer accounts and made 286 unauthorised transactions totalling about $490,000, hitting 87 separate Alliance Bank customers. The bank reimbursed all affected customers.
title: APRA wins $8 million penalty against Bendigo Bank over 2023 cyber incident

evidence.quote: pays a pecuniary penalty of $8 million in respect of its contraventions of the BEAR, subject to Court approval.
gain access to approximately 257 customer accounts

validation.note: APRA's own release (11 Aug 2026, proposed penalty and incident figures) and Mirage News (24 Nov 2026, court order) read. The APRA page read is the August release; the court-outcome release was not read.

review.note: stronger than the source: exec/plain said regulated entities must have appropriate protection; now APRA expects robust cyber protection systems (Mirage). Figures, date, status checked against APRA and Mirage
